name: Multilingual Transcription Engine
tagline: Accurate transcripts in every language served
shortDescription: Telephony-grade speech-to-text that converts 100% of your recorded calls into searchable, speaker-separated transcripts across 40+ languages and dialects.
longDescription:
Most contact centers review fewer than 5% of their calls because transcription has always been the bottleneck: too slow, too expensive, too inaccurate on real telephony audio. The Multilingual Transcription Engine removes that bottleneck. Upload recordings in batch or stream them through the API, and every call becomes a clean, timestamped, speaker-separated transcript — typically faster than 2x real time.

The engine is tuned for the audio call centers actually have: 8kHz lines, crosstalk, hold music, IVR fragments, and customers who switch languages mid-sentence. Automatic language detection and code-switching support mean a call that starts in English and shifts to Spanish stays coherent in one transcript, correctly attributed to each speaker.

Domain lexicons let you teach the engine your product names, policy codes, and industry vocabulary, so 'HSA rollover' never becomes 'H.S. hey rollover.' Built-in PCI and PII redaction scrubs card numbers and personal identifiers before transcripts ever reach a reviewer's screen — protecting customers and keeping your QA program audit-ready.

Every downstream Homayar module — scoring, sentiment, intent, coaching — builds on this foundation. When the transcript layer is right, everything above it gets sharper.
whoItsFor: Call-center operations leaders and enterprise IT teams who need every call converted to reliable text — especially organizations serving multilingual customer bases or operating under compliance requirements.

95%+ word accuracy on 8kHz telephony audio

Reviewer prep time cut from 12 minutes per call to zero

name: Acoustic Emotion & Sentiment Analysis
tagline: Measure how every customer actually feels
shortDescription: Combines acoustic signals — pitch, pace, energy, silence — with transcript sentiment to track customer and agent emotional state second by second through every call.
longDescription:
Words tell half the story. A customer can say 'fine' in a way that means anything but. Acoustic Emotion & Sentiment Analysis listens to both layers: what was said, and how it was said. By fusing prosodic features — pitch variance, speaking rate, vocal energy, interruptions, and dead air — with transcript-level sentiment, it produces an emotion timeline for every call, both sides of the conversation.

Supervisors see exactly where a call turned: the moment frustration spiked, the de-escalation that worked, the long silence after a price was quoted. Instead of vague labels like 'negative call,' you get a navigable timeline — click any emotional inflection point and the audio plays from that second.

The same lens applies to agents, framed as support rather than scrutiny. Rising agent stress across a shift is an early signal for burnout and attrition. Teams use these patterns to adjust schedules, route tougher call types to senior staff, and time coaching conversations before performance dips — a companion for the people on the phones, not a camera over their shoulder.

Emotion data flows into every other Homayar module: QA scorecards can weight empathy criteria with acoustic evidence, CSAT prediction sharpens, and escalation alerts trigger on emotional trajectory rather than keywords alone.
whoItsFor: CX and QA managers who need to understand emotional dynamics at scale, and operations leaders monitoring team wellbeing and escalation patterns across thousands of calls.

Escalation moments pinpointed to within 3 seconds of onset
30-40% faster call review via emotion-driven navigation
Early burnout signals surfaced weeks before attrition events
Empathy scoring backed by acoustic evidence, not reviewer guesswork

name: Topic & Intent Discovery
shortDescription: Unsupervised topic clustering and intent classification that turns thousands of unstructured calls into a ranked, trending map of why customers actually contact you.
longDescription:
Ask three department heads why customers call and you'll get three different answers — all anecdotal. Topic & Intent Discovery replaces opinion with measurement. Specialized AI agents read every transcript, cluster conversations into topics, classify caller intent, and rank everything by volume, trend, handle time, and emotional charge.

The system discovers topics you didn't know to look for. A new billing-page bug shows up as an emerging cluster within hours, not as a quarterly-review surprise. A confusing policy change reveals itself as a fast-growing intent with above-average handle time and below-average sentiment. You define nothing upfront; the taxonomy emerges from the calls themselves, then becomes editable so business language stays consistent.

For planning teams, this is the missing demand signal. Deflection programs get built around the top self-serviceable intents. Training curricula target the topics with the worst first-call resolution. Product teams receive a weekly digest of what customers struggle with, quoted verbatim from real conversations — evidence, not anecdotes.

Every topic links back to its underlying calls, so any number on the dashboard is two clicks from the actual customer voice behind it.
whoItsFor: Operations leaders sizing deflection and staffing opportunities, and CX or product teams who need a ground-truth answer to 'what are customers actually contacting us about?'

name: Automated QA Scorecards
tagline: Score every call against your standards
shortDescription: AI agents evaluate 100% of calls against your existing QA scorecard — greeting, verification, compliance, resolution, empathy — with evidence cited for every score.
longDescription:
Manual QA reviews 2-5% of calls and takes a week to do it. Automated QA Scorecards evaluates all of them, usually within minutes of the recording landing. You bring your existing scorecard — the criteria your QA team already trusts — and Homayar's evaluation agents apply it consistently to every conversation, every day.

Each criterion gets more than a pass/fail. The system cites its evidence: the exact transcript segment where identity verification happened (or didn't), the timestamp where the required disclosure was read, the exchange that justified the empathy score. Reviewers stop hunting through 20-minute recordings and start verifying targeted moments. Most teams find a reviewer's throughput triples while their judgment stays firmly in the loop.

Compliance-critical criteria can be set to zero-tolerance: a missed disclosure or skipped verification flags the call for human review within minutes, not at month-end when the regulatory exposure has already compounded. Auto-fail patterns that took weeks to surface now page a supervisor the same morning.

Scores roll up by agent, team, queue, and criterion, so coaching conversations start from trends across hundreds of calls rather than one unlucky sample. The framing matters: agents see their own dashboards, their best calls get flagged as exemplars, and the scorecard becomes a shared standard instead of a monthly verdict.
whoItsFor: QA managers and compliance officers who need full-coverage evaluation without scaling headcount, and operations leaders replacing sample-based QA with population-level quality data.

name: Calibration Workspace
tagline: Align every reviewer on one standard
shortDescription: A structured workspace for QA calibration sessions: blind scoring rounds, variance analytics, AI-vs-human alignment tracking, and a documented decision log for every criterion.
longDescription:
Every QA leader knows the quiet problem: the same call scored by three reviewers gets three different numbers. Calibration sessions are supposed to fix this, but they run on spreadsheets, screen-shares, and whoever argues loudest. The Calibration Workspace turns calibration into an instrumented process.

Session leads pick calls — randomly, by disputed score, or by AI/human disagreement — and reviewers score them blind, without seeing each other's marks or the AI's evaluation. The workspace then reveals everything at once: per-criterion variance, each reviewer's drift from the group, and exactly where the AI's interpretation diverged from the team's. Discussion happens where the data says it should, not where opinions are strongest.

Every resolution becomes a documented precedent. When the team decides what 'acknowledged the customer's frustration' actually requires, that decision is recorded against the criterion, with the example call attached, and feeds back into how Homayar's evaluation agents score going forward. The AI calibrates to your team's standard — not the other way around.

Over time, the workspace becomes the institutional memory of your quality program: a searchable history of every scoring decision, ready for auditor questions, new-reviewer onboarding, and the inevitable 'why did this call get an 82?'
whoItsFor: QA program leads and quality directors running multi-reviewer teams or BPO partnerships, where score consistency across evaluators is contractually or operationally critical.

name: Dispute & Appeal Workflow
shortDescription: A transparent appeal process for QA scores: agents contest with evidence, reviewers respond against the recording, and every outcome feeds back into scoring accuracy.
longDescription:
A QA program agents don't trust is a QA program that doesn't change behavior. When scores feel arbitrary and there's no recourse, agents disengage from feedback entirely — and the quality data quietly loses its meaning. The Dispute & Appeal Workflow gives every score a fair, fast, documented path to challenge.

An agent who disagrees with a score files an appeal directly from their scorecard, pointing to the specific criterion and the moment in the call they believe was misjudged. The reviewer — or a designated second evaluator — responds against the same evidence: the transcript, the audio, the criterion definition, and any calibration precedents on record. No hallway debates, no he-said-she-said. The recording settles it.

Every resolution is tracked. Appeals upheld against AI-scored criteria automatically flow into Homayar's scoring feedback loop, improving future accuracy. Appeals upheld against human reviewers surface as calibration topics. Patterns — one criterion drawing 30% of all disputes, one team appealing at triple the rate — show leaders exactly where the scorecard or the training needs work.

This is the companion philosophy made concrete: a quality system with due process built in. Teams that deploy it consistently report higher feedback acceptance, lower grievance escalations, and agents who engage with QA results instead of bracing against them.
whoItsFor: QA managers and HR-adjacent operations leaders in unionized, regulated, or high-attrition environments where score fairness directly affects engagement and retention.

name: CSAT Prediction
tagline: Predicted satisfaction for every single call
shortDescription: Models trained on your survey responses predict a CSAT score for every call — including the 90%+ of customers who never answer a survey.
longDescription:
Survey response rates in most contact centers sit between 5% and 15%, and the customers who respond skew toward the very happy and the very angry. Every CSAT number on your dashboard is built on that thin, biased slice. CSAT Prediction fills in the rest: a satisfaction score for every call, modeled from the conversation itself.

The system learns from your own ground truth. Calls that did receive survey responses become training signal, mapping conversational features — resolution language, emotional trajectory, hold patterns, repeat-contact markers — to actual scores your customers gave. The result is a per-call prediction with a confidence band, validated continuously against incoming survey data so you can see precisely how well it tracks reality.

With full coverage, satisfaction becomes operational instead of retrospective. A predicted-detractor call triggers a same-day callback while the relationship is still recoverable. A queue whose predicted CSAT slides mid-week gets attention Wednesday, not in next month's review. Team and site comparisons rest on tens of thousands of data points rather than a few hundred survey replies.

For agents, predicted CSAT works as a companion metric: visibility into how their conversations likely landed, on every call, without waiting for the survey lottery. Coaching gets anchored to specific, recent, representative interactions.
whoItsFor: CX leaders accountable for satisfaction targets, and operations managers who need satisfaction signal on every interaction — not just the few customers who answer surveys.

name: Churn Risk Signals
tagline: Catch at-risk customers before they leave
shortDescription: Detects cancellation language, competitor mentions, unresolved-issue patterns, and emotional trajectories across calls to flag accounts at risk of churn — with enough lead time to act.
longDescription:
Customers rarely leave without telling you first. They tell you in calls: a competitor's name dropped casually, a third contact about the same unresolved issue, a shift in tone from frustrated to flat. Churn Risk Signals listens for these patterns across every conversation and turns them into account-level risk scores your retention team can actually work.

The model goes beyond keyword spotting. A single 'thinking about switching' matters less than the trajectory: rising contact frequency, declining sentiment across consecutive calls, escalations that ended without resolution language, requests for contract terms or cancellation policies. Signals compound at the account level, so a customer whose last three calls each looked routine in isolation still surfaces when the pattern across them does not.

Risk scores flow to your CRM with the evidence attached — the specific calls, quotes, and unresolved issues behind each flag — so retention outreach starts informed rather than generic. Win-back offers reach customers while the decision is still forming, which is where save rates are won.

For enterprises, the deployment is tailored: risk models tuned to your churn definitions and renewal cycles, integration with your CRM and customer-data platform, and thresholds calibrated against your historical churn cohorts. Engagement is scoped with your team, including on-premise and VPC deployment options.
whoItsFor: Retention and CX leaders at subscription, contract, or relationship-revenue businesses — telecoms, insurers, banks, and SaaS companies — where saving an account is far cheaper than replacing it.

name: Journey Friction Audit
tagline: Find where your customer journeys break
shortDescription: A one-time, fixed-scope analysis of 60 days of call recordings that maps repeat contacts, transfers, and failed self-service into a ranked, evidence-backed friction report.
longDescription:
No customer journey map survives contact with reality. The flows on the whiteboard say 'customer calls, issue resolved'; the calls themselves say 'customer called twice, was transferred three times, repeated their account number to four people, and mentioned the broken web form each time.' The Journey Friction Audit builds the map from the evidence.

You provide 60 days of call recordings; Homayar's analysis agents stitch interactions into journeys — repeat contacts about the same issue, transfers within calls, references to failed self-service attempts ('I tried the app first'), and explicit effort language ('this is the third time I'm calling'). Each journey stage receives a friction score built from contact recurrence, resolution latency, transfer depth, and customer-stated effort.

The deliverable is a ranked friction report with an executive readout. Maybe 18% of billing calls reference a failed portal payment first — that's a quantified business case for the digital team, with call evidence attached. Maybe transfers between two specific departments add four minutes and a sentiment drop on every occurrence — that's a routing fix with a measurable payoff. Friction stops being a workshop topic and becomes a prioritized backlog.

The engagement is fixed-price and fixed-timeline: recordings in, findings delivered within 15 business days, no subscription required. Many teams repeat the audit annually to verify their fixes moved the numbers — same methodology, year over year.
whoItsFor: CX strategy and operations executives who need hard call evidence to prioritize self-service, routing, and process fixes — or an independent benchmark before funding a journey program.
